<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Summary

Add an opt-in FlyDSL MoE backend for ROCm gfx942, using [ROCm/aiter#6995](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6995). It keeps checkpoint MXFP4 weights and BF16 activations, and implements the model's clamped SiLU with BF16 rounding before activation. Existing defaults and backend priorities do not change.

Select it with `--moe-backend aiter_flydsl_mxfp4_bf16`. A supported AITER build containing the new API is required; the global dependency image is not updated by this PR.

## How Much Faster?

**The measured complete MoE operator is 3.15x faster at M8 and 2.50x at M32 than the pinned vLLM unfused implementation.** At the larger measured batches, the improvement is 1.53x-1.91x. These are operator results, not full-model serving speedups.

Target: MI325X/gfx942, H=5120, logical intermediate=288 padded to 384, 384 experts, top-6, clamp=10. M is token rows entering one TP-local MoE call, not client concurrency. Same inputs and weights; seed 101/uniform routing; five timed passes per candidate; median GPU kernel time:

| Token rows M | Before: vLLM unfused (us) | After: automatic AITER dispatch (us) | Operator speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 242.419 | 76.988 | **3.15x** |
| 32 | 496.073 | 198.185 | **2.50x** |
| 128 | 950.240 | 501.539 | **1.89x** |
| 512 | 1094.238 | 572.864 | **1.91x** |
| 4096 | 2233.506 | 1463.233 | **1.53x** |

Speedup = before/after latency. The measurement includes sorting, both GEMMs, activation and output reduction/zeroing; it excludes router scoring, shared experts, TP communication, attention and host launch gaps. It uses reused weights, not a cold-weight or full-model CUDA Graph protocol.

**Where the gain comes from:** the complete AITER MoE implementation is faster than the unfused comparator. Within that AITER implementation, the two qualified CSV entries add another **1.61x at M8** and **1.25x at M32** versus its same-math default tiles. Only those exact gfx942/304-CU shape keys select tuned tiles; unmatched batches keep the defaults. This is not a claim that adding clamp alone makes an existing kernel 3x faster. Across 12 decode holdouts, 11 established a strict timing margin; one M32 hot-routing case did not. No decode regression was detected in those holdouts.

These are the recorded earlier operator measurements using AITER `f52deef`; they were not rerun after the latest vLLM main merge. Source versions and the unchanged original measurements are retained below.

## Accuracy And Correctness

**No score decrease was observed in the paired 200-question GSM8K subset.** The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint loaded at TP8, with the selected backend verified on all 40 layers of every rank.

| Backend | Correct / 200 | Accuracy | Truncated | Empty / invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `triton_unfused` | 196 / 200 | 98.0% | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| `aiter_flydsl_mxfp4_bf16` | 197 / 200 | 98.5% | 1 | 0 / 0 |

Same first 200 test questions, 5-shot prompts, greedy seed 0, thinking disabled, batches of 8, max 512 output tokens. Both runs exited 0. Paired outcomes: 196 both correct, 3 both wrong, 1 gained, 0 lost; the same question was truncated. Text changed on 137 questions. This single subset run is **not bitwise equivalence, proof of lossless accuracy, or evidence of general accuracy improvement**; the full 1,319-question set was not run.

All 15 synthetic numerical cases and 24 sampled real-checkpoint layer cases passed their stated gates. Automatic dispatch had maximum NRMSE 0.3723% versus the pinned vLLM expert and 0.4111% versus the sampled FP32 reference. Real-layer NRMSE was 0.3619%-0.4125%. BF16 atomic accumulation is not bitwise deterministic.

## Scope And Readiness

- Supported: gfx942, BF16 activations, native MXFP4 weights, clamped unit-slope SiLU, TP without EP; no bias, LoRA, EPLB or MonoKernel. Weights are not requantized to INT4.
- Latest merged-source tests: **5/5 passed** with the pinned new AITER API, including real Quark `LLM` loading/generation; **5/5 passed** for stock-AITER rejection. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. This is local source-snapshot validation with previously installed compiled libraries, not hosted CI or a clean matching rebuild.
- Full-model GSM8K used 32 GiB CPU offload per GPU, CPU-resident Engram and eager execution alongside an unchanged resident service. Its elapsed evaluation time is **not** normal GPU-resident serving-performance evidence.
- Remaining gates: supported AITER release/image integration and matching-binary validation. Full-model graph execution, normal GPU-resident serving performance and full GSM8K accuracy remain unvalidated.

AI assistance: GitHub Copilot. This edit reorganizes existing evidence; no new tests or performance measurements are claimed.

Most of these can't fail once the oracle has selected this class:
- `activation != SILU`: rejected by `_supports_activation`.
- `expert_map` / `expert_tokens_meta`: `_supports_parallel_config` forbids EP, and the no-DP/EP prepare returns no metadata.
- `a1q_scale` / `a2_scale`: the scheme is `(kMxfp4Static, None)`, so inputs are never quantized.
- `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0`: `FusedMoEKernel._fused_experts` returns early when `M_full == 0` (`modular_kernel.py:1350`), so `apply` never sees zero tokens.

Only `apply_router_weight_on_input` isn't checked at selection. The same applies to `__init__`, where bias and clamp were already checked against `moe_config` and `flydsl_a16w4_moe` re-checks the clamp, and to `num_local_experts != num_experts` in `is_supported_config`, which no-EP already implies. Suggest keeping `is_supported_config` as the single check, plus `apply_router_weight_on_input` here, with `self.clamp_limit = moe_config.swiglu_limit`.

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Summary

Add an opt-in FlyDSL MoE backend for ROCm gfx942, using [ROCm/aiter#6995](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6995). It keeps checkpoint MXFP4 weights and BF16 activations, and implements the model's clamped SiLU with BF16 rounding before activation. Existing defaults and backend priorities do not change.

Select it with `--moe-backend aiter_flydsl_mxfp4_bf16`. A supported AITER build containing the new API is required; the global dependency image is not updated by this PR.

## How Much Faster?

**The measured complete MoE operator is 3.15x faster at M8 and 2.50x at M32 than the pinned vLLM unfused implementation.** At the larger measured batches, the improvement is 1.53x-1.91x. These are operator results, not full-model serving speedups.

Target: MI325X/gfx942, H=5120, logical intermediate=288 padded to 384, 384 experts, top-6, clamp=10. M is token rows entering one TP-local MoE call, not client concurrency. Same inputs and weights; seed 101/uniform routing; five timed passes per candidate; median GPU kernel time:

| Token rows M | Before: vLLM unfused (us) | After: automatic AITER dispatch (us) | Operator speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 242.419 | 76.988 | **3.15x** |
| 32 | 496.073 | 198.185 | **2.50x** |
| 128 | 950.240 | 501.539 | **1.89x** |
| 512 | 1094.238 | 572.864 | **1.91x** |
| 4096 | 2233.506 | 1463.233 | **1.53x** |

Speedup = before/after latency. The measurement includes sorting, both GEMMs, activation and output reduction/zeroing; it excludes router scoring, shared experts, TP communication, attention and host launch gaps. It uses reused weights, not a cold-weight or full-model CUDA Graph protocol.

**Where the gain comes from:** the complete AITER MoE implementation is faster than the unfused comparator. Within that AITER implementation, the two qualified CSV entries add another **1.61x at M8** and **1.25x at M32** versus its same-math default tiles. Only those exact gfx942/304-CU shape keys select tuned tiles; unmatched batches keep the defaults. This is not a claim that adding clamp alone makes an existing kernel 3x faster. Across 12 decode holdouts, 11 established a strict timing margin; one M32 hot-routing case did not. No decode regression was detected in those holdouts.

These are the recorded earlier operator measurements using AITER `f52deef`; they were not rerun after the latest vLLM main merge. Source versions and the unchanged original measurements are retained below.

## Accuracy And Correctness

**No score decrease was observed in the paired 200-question GSM8K subset.** The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint loaded at TP8, with the selected backend verified on all 40 layers of every rank.

| Backend | Correct / 200 | Accuracy | Truncated | Empty / invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `triton_unfused` | 196 / 200 | 98.0% | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| `aiter_flydsl_mxfp4_bf16` | 197 / 200 | 98.5% | 1 | 0 / 0 |

Same first 200 test questions, 5-shot prompts, greedy seed 0, thinking disabled, batches of 8, max 512 output tokens. Both runs exited 0. Paired outcomes: 196 both correct, 3 both wrong, 1 gained, 0 lost; the same question was truncated. Text changed on 137 questions. This single subset run is **not bitwise equivalence, proof of lossless accuracy, or evidence of general accuracy improvement**; the full 1,319-question set was not run.

All 15 synthetic numerical cases and 24 sampled real-checkpoint layer cases passed their stated gates. Automatic dispatch had maximum NRMSE 0.3723% versus the pinned vLLM expert and 0.4111% versus the sampled FP32 reference. Real-layer NRMSE was 0.3619%-0.4125%. BF16 atomic accumulation is not bitwise deterministic.

## Scope And Readiness

- Supported: gfx942, BF16 activations, native MXFP4 weights, clamped unit-slope SiLU, TP without EP; no bias, LoRA, EPLB or MonoKernel. Weights are not requantized to INT4.
- Latest merged-source tests: **5/5 passed** with the pinned new AITER API, including real Quark `LLM` loading/generation; **5/5 passed** for stock-AITER rejection. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. This is local source-snapshot validation with previously installed compiled libraries, not hosted CI or a clean matching rebuild.
- Full-model GSM8K used 32 GiB CPU offload per GPU, CPU-resident Engram and eager execution alongside an unchanged resident service. Its elapsed evaluation time is **not** normal GPU-resident serving-performance evidence.
- Remaining gates: supported AITER release/image integration and matching-binary validation. Full-model graph execution, normal GPU-resident serving performance and full GSM8K accuracy remain unvalidated.

AI assistance: GitHub Copilot. This edit reorganizes existing evidence; no new tests or performance measurements are claimed.

## Validation

Current Python source base: `335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1`.
Earlier performance and full-model results used base
`5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9` plus the initial integration.

Review-fix commit: `8ddca5da6433c8fd7e53b8ad52110e07d5f5ffcf`.
Conflict-resolution merge: `ef768ca7877c4cde2233447c586a28475b3b8117`.
At draft creation, the branch was one commit ahead and 275 commits behind
upstream `main`; the initial comparison contained five reviewed files.
The review-fix commit added a scoped AMD hardware CI job. The merge retains
the existing PR commits and updates to current `main` without force-pushing.
AITER: `f52deefccdb66c410b337a2947050b228a55e547`, FlyDSL 0.4.0. MI325X/gfx942.
Source-snapshot tests use compiled libraries from vLLM `00b6c4c56`; these are
not clean rebuilt-wheel results. Revalidation with matching binaries is a
remaining readiness gate, not a completed check.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -x tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \
  -k aiter_flydsl

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  .buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml \
  vllm/config/kernel.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md
```

Result with the pinned new API: **5 passed**, covering M0/M1/M8/M33, explicit
oracle selection, weight conversion, rejected configurations, modular
prepare/expert/finalize, BF16 reference math, CUDA graph replay and a real
one-layer Quark checkpoint through `LLM` loading and generation.
`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was set. Starting with both AITER flags disabled
now works, and fixture teardown restores the environment and cached flags.
Applicable pre-commit hooks passed with exit 0, including mypy, formatting
and test tethering.

### Conflict Resolution (2026-10-30)

- The sole content conflict was in `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml`:
  upstream replaced the old `ci_base` flow with two image-build steps at the
  insertion point of the new gfx942 test job. The resolution preserves both
  upstream build steps and the PR's test job unchanged.
- YAML structural comparisons verify unchanged job definitions, unique keys
  and complete dependencies; the test job passes `bash -n`.
- On the merged Python tree, pinned-AITER positive tests passed **5/5**
  (52.54 s), including the real Quark `LLM` regression. Stock-AITER rejection
  tests passed **5/5** (5.23 s). Both AITER flags started disabled and
  `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was enabled.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed for all six PR files. Their contents
  match the validated snapshot. The merged tree differs from current main
  only in these six files. This is source-snapshot validation with the
  previously installed compiled libraries, not a clean matching rebuild or
  a new full-model quality/performance evaluation.

### Review Follow-Up (2026-10-30)

- Reuse the native converter from Quark's converter entrypoint instead of
  registering a backend that later fails during weight loading.
- The new seeded H256/I384/E8/top6 Quark model regression loads real MXFP4
  weights through `LLM`, asserts the selected expert class, and compares four
  greedy tokens and their logprobs with `triton_unfused`.
- Running that test with only the converter fix reverted fails with
  `ValueError: Unsupported mxfp4_backend: Mxfp4MoeBackend.AITER_FLYDSL_MXFP4_BF16`;
  restoring the fix passes. Reproduction command:
  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -x tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_aiter_flydsl_mxfp4_quark_loading`.
- Older AITER builds now exercise explicit missing-capability rejection
  assertions, not a skip. The new gfx942 hardware job first checks the base
  dependency, then installs official AITER commit `f52deef` and FlyDSL 0.4.0
  into an isolated environment, requires the API to exist and reruns the
  positive tests. `AITER_USE_SYSTEM_TRITON=1` preserves the image's matching
  Triton installation. The global AITER image pin is unchanged.
- Executing the exact job locally on gfx942 completed with exit 0: **5 passed**
  for the old-dependency rejection phase and **5 passed** for the pinned-API
  positive phase. This is local execution of the job, not a hosted CI result.

</details>

<summary>Original operator and model evaluation evidence (earlier integration)</summary>

### Earlier Performance And Model Evidence

Fresh same-input operator measurements, H5120/I384(logical288)/E384/top6,
clamp10, five passes per candidate, seed101/uniform, kernel-time medians:

| M | Pinned vLLM unfused us | Same-math AITER default us | Automatic AITER CSV us [min, max] |

| 4096 | 2233.506 | 1459.061 | 1463.233 [1462.417, 1465.943] |

Across 12 decode holdouts, same-math kernel speedups were 1.590x-1.707x at M8
and 1.080x-1.250x at M32. Eleven cleared the strict kernel/event separated-range
gate; one M32 hot-routing case did not establish a stable margin. No decode
regression was detected. Only M8/M32 match the CSV; larger batches retain the
default tiles. These microbenchmarks do not measure vLLM serving.

Numerical checks passed on all 15 synthetic cases. For the automatic
`flydsl_dispatch` candidate, max NRMSE vs the pinned vLLM expert was 0.3723%;
maximum sampled FP32-reference NRMSE was 0.4111%.
Twenty-four real-checkpoint layer cases (three layers, endpoint TP8 ranks,
eight sampled experts, two batches and two synthetic input scales) passed;
CSV NRMSE was 0.3619%-0.4125%. This does not replace a full-model evaluation.

Full-model validation (2026-10-30): the real `LLM` entrypoint loaded
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint `314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6`
at TP8. Every rank reported the expected expert backend on all 40 layers.
Both configurations generated `12`, `54` and a coherent compiler explanation,
then completed the same first 200 GSM8K test questions with the first five
training examples as 5-shot context, greedy seed 0, thinking disabled,
batches of 8 and maximum 512 output tokens. Prompt construction and scoring
reuse `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` through offline `LLM.chat`.

| Backend | Correct / 200 | Accuracy | Truncated | Empty / Invalid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton_unfused | 196 | 98.0% | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| aiter_flydsl_mxfp4_bf16 | 197 | 98.5% | 1 | 0 / 0 |

Both runs exited 0. Prompt/label digest and all per-question prompt hashes
matched. Paired audit: 196 both correct, 3 both wrong, 1 gained, 0 lost; the same
question was truncated in both. Text differed on 137 questions, so this is not
bitwise equivalence. This small single-run subset does not establish general
accuracy superiority and is not the full 1,319-question GSM8K evaluation.

The complete model ran alongside an unchanged resident service using 32 GiB
CPU offload per GPU, CPU-resident Engram, GPU-memory budget 0.10, eager mode,
max length 2048, prefill budget 256 and fp8_ds_mla KV cache. Evaluation elapsed
was 913.513 s baseline versus 565.748 s candidate, but these are offload timings,
not representative GPU-resident serving-performance evidence.

**Remaining readiness gates:** a supported AITER release/global image integration
containing #6995 and revalidation with matching binaries. The isolated test
job pins the candidate API but does not close those release gates. Full-model graph
execution, normal GPU-resident serving performance and the full GSM8K test set
remain unvalidated; hosted CI success is not claimed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and review provenance</summary>

## Details

Open-PR searches used `FlyDSL`, `mxfp4`, `FlyDSL MoE`, `gfx942 mxfp4`,
`6995 in:body` and `silu_clamped`. No exact adapter duplicate was found.
Inspected #51563 covers groupwise INT4 API migration, #50817 targets Kimi
gfx942 paths, #64084 targets Muse Spark through AITER Triton W4A16, and #59766
covers bias-free GPT-OSS SwiGLU correctness. None is the new explicit
clamped-SiLU/BF16-rounding API adapter in this patch.

The implementation stays in the existing AITER expert module, MXFP4 oracle,
backend config, existing MXFP4 tests and rendered MoE guide. A dedicated
gfx942 hardware job now covers both dependency states and Quark loading.
Weights are not requantized to INT4. BF16 atomic top-k accumulation is not
bitwise deterministic. MonoKernel and EP are outside the supported scope.

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used to implement the patch and execute
the recorded checks. On 2026-10-30, the submitting author confirmed reviewing
and personally testing the initial integration, then requested this single
review-fix commit and the subsequent conflict resolution. Follow-up and merge
validation results above were executed with AI assistance.

Most of these can't fail once the oracle has selected this class:
- `activation != SILU`: rejected by `_supports_activation`.
- `expert_map` / `expert_tokens_meta`: `_supports_parallel_config` forbids EP, and the no-DP/EP prepare returns no metadata.
- `a1q_scale` / `a2_scale`: the scheme is `(kMxfp4Static, None)`, so inputs are never quantized.
- `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0`: `FusedMoEKernel._fused_experts` returns early when `M_full == 0` (`modular_kernel.py:1350`), so `apply` never sees zero tokens.

Only `apply_router_weight_on_input` isn't checked at selection. The same applies to `__init__`, where bias and clamp were already checked against `moe_config` and `flydsl_a16w4_moe` re-checks the clamp, and to `num_local_experts != num_experts` in `is_supported_config`, which no-EP already implies. Suggest keeping `is_supported_config` as the single check, plus `apply_router_weight_on_input` here, with `self.clamp_limit = moe_config.swiglu_limit`.
